newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, marks and yen down.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, marks and yen down.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed, with marks and yen holding slim losses while June sterling ended near the session high in extremely thin volume, traders said.
"The market is devoid of interest," one forex trader said about the futures and cash trade. "We've cleaned out weak (dollar) longs, but when the dollar's uptrend resumes remains to be seen."
Another floor broker said the dollar was in a "range funk" of 1.6950 to 1.7100 spot marks, or about $0.5935 to $0.5883 in June marks.
Another trader said dollar/mark would have to hit 1.6650 spot, or about $0.6042 in June marks, to break the dollar's uptrend.
Activity was light in the mark pit, with the largest trade occurring around mid-morning when one firm sold 1,300 June to September spreads, a trader said.
June marks limited losses due to overnight comments Bundesbank official Franz-Christoph Zeitler. Zeitler said there was no current need for a rate change.
One trader said comments from other Bundesbank officials regarding the European Monetary Union also supported marks.
Several Bundesbank officials insisted the 1999 EMU launch date must be met, taking a softer approach on the Maastricht criteria.

Gains in sterling futures largely reflected the currency's advance against the mark rather than the dollar. However, some traders said the dollar's ability to rise slightly against marks indirectly boosted sterling against the German currency.
June sterling closed up $0.0042 at $1.6054, near the session high of $1.6058.
They said late bids in the yen pit supported June yen near the upper end of the day's range.
"Japan nuclear disaster (news) didn't do much to yen," a floor broker said about the overnight small fire at a Japanese nuclear fuel processing plant 100 miles northeast of Tokyo.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000013 at $0.008321, marks were down $0.0009 to $0.5905, Swiss francs fell $0.0003 to $0.6862, sterling was up $0.0042 to $1.6054, Canadian dollars were up $0.0017 to $0.7361, Australian dollars were up $0.0044 at $0.7919, and Mexican pesos were $0.000250 lower at $0.119875.
